clue.text: Affectionate type meeting assailant in secret

parts.note: someone affectionate who embraces people is a hugger
a mugger is a street attacker who robs people

explanation.surface: A cuddly person secretly meets someone who attacks them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' simply joins the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming old phrase describes concealed, clandestine dealings, so it serves as an adverbial synonym for secretly.

clue.text: Cry of praise from house physician finally touring hospital area

indicators.note: touring here means visiting, so the letter goes on a tour inside the other pieces

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the word physician

explanation.surface: A junior hospital doctor is making ward rounds around a hospital district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house physician' looks like one phrase, a junior hospital doctor, but splits: 'house' gives its abbreviation and 'finally' takes the last letter of 'physician', which 'touring' places within the hospital and area letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew exclamation is shouted in worship, notably on Palm Sunday, as an expression of adoration.

clue.text: Splendid warning about duke concerning historic resting-place

parts.note: great can mean splendid, as in a great time

indicators.note: about means the warning word goes round the other letters

parts.note: beware is a warning cry, as on a sign
of can mean concerning, as in tales of adventure

explanation.surface: A grand caution about an aristocrat regarding an old place of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Bed of Ware is a huge Elizabethan four-poster bed, mentioned by Shakespeare and now in the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This famously enormous antique bed is a celebrated historic object for sleeping in, hence a resting-place from history.

clue.text: Passage from book throws out court especially

indicators.note: throws out tells us to remove the court abbreviation from the longer word

parts.note: an extract is a passage taken from a book

explanation.surface: A reading from a book dismisses a court case in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra used as an adverb means especially or unusually, as in being extra careful.

clue.text: The French copper penetrating spy's part of compound

indicators.note: penetrating says these letters push into the middle of the spy word

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation; the 's is a link meaning has
le is the French masculine word for the
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A French policeman infiltrates a secret agent's part of a walled compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU; LE and CU go inside MOLE as MO-LECU-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical compound is made of molecules, each a group of bonded atoms, so a molecule is a part of one.

clue.text: Impress leader of group supported by 12

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts the first piece above the second
leader of points to only the opening letter of the word group

parts.note: 12 across is the politician's surname; Rab Butler was a leading Conservative minister, so the cross-reference gives his first name

explanation.surface: Win over the head of a team who is backed by a well-known statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' places G on top of RAB in this down entry. 12 is BUTLER, and RAB Butler was a senior British Conservative politician of the mid-20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Impress in its old sense means seize or press into service, and grab means to seize, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Legal appointee's without ploys reportedly involving old currency

indicators.note: involving means the outer letters wrap round the currency

parts.note: ex is a Latin word meaning without or out of, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a spelling that sounds like the word for ploys

parts.note: tricks are ploys or stratagems
the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro

explanation.surface: A lawyer's appointee, said to be without schemes, deals in an obsolete currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives a spelling that sounds like the word for ploys; 'involving' wraps the first and third pieces round the currency. The 's of 'appointee's' means is.
explanation.definitionFit: An executrix is a woman appointed under a will to carry out its provisions, a legal role.

clue.text: It's very monotonous and said to be bad for one's shoes

indicators.note: said to be signals that the phrase sounds the same as the entry when spoken

parts.note: something that wears out the soles of footwear would be sole-destroying

explanation.surface: A dull job is described as wearing out one's footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLE and SOUL sound the same, so 'sole-destroying' (ruining shoe soles) gives the spelling for a deadening task.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is soul-destroying is so dull and repetitive it crushes the spirit, hence extremely tedious.

clue.text: Much loved illustrator engaged in publicity

indicators.note: engaged in means the artist is placed inside the publicity word

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a piece of publicity
Gustave Doré was a famous French book illustrator

explanation.surface: A beloved artist takes part in an advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illustrator' points to a specific artist, Gustave Doré, rather than a generic word; 'engaged in' splits the publicity word around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply, worshipped, so it is a direct synonym for much loved.

clue.text: Got a whiff of 23

definitions.meaning: past tense of the verb meaning to sense with the nose
23 down is the cross-reference for a sea creature; a small food fish

explanation.definitionFit: Smelt is the British past tense of smell, and separately a small silvery edible fish.

clue.text: Tenure he rejected in meadow exchanged for cash

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the selling word

parts.note: sold means exchanged for money

indicators.note: rejected means the little word he is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A property right that he turned down is sold off as a field for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns 'he' backwards, and 'in' sets that inside the word for sold; 'meadow' leads the charade. 'exchanged for cash' is one piece, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold is a form of land tenure in which property is held under a lease for a fixed term.

clue.text: Bird originally nesting under roofing material

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letters of the words nesting and under

parts.note: thatch is straw or reeds used to roof a building

explanation.surface: A bird first nests beneath the straw of a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of both 'nesting' and 'under', N and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small European tree-climbing songbird that can walk down trunks headfirst.

clue.text: British novelist in charge of port?

definitions.meaning: Samuel ..., English author of Erewhon and The Way of All Flesh
a household servant who looks after the wine cellar, including the port

explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts a harbour reading, but it is the fortified wine the servant guards; the question mark flags this description by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler was an English Victorian novelist, and a butler is the chief manservant who keeps the wine.

clue.text: Responsive girl involved in leisurely walk

indicators.note: involved in means the name is placed inside the walking word

parts.note: an amble is a slow relaxed walk
Ena is a girl's name, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: An agreeable young woman joins a gentle stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts the girl's name inside the stroll word, splitting it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means open to suggestion and willing to cooperate, so readily responsive.

clue.text: Course in Holy Writ upset Herod at first

indicators.note: at first tells us the ruler's name comes before the other piece

parts.note: Herod Antipas was the ruler of Galilee in the Gospels

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the scripture letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is part of Holy Writ

explanation.surface: A passage of scripture turned King Herod's stomach in the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herod' points to his family name ANTIPAS; 'upset' reverses OT to TO. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables, a course served before the main meal.

clue.text: Enthusiast welcoming monarch in China?

indicators.note: welcoming means the enthusiast word takes the monarch letter inside it

parts.note: a fiend is an addict or devotee, as in a fresh-air fiend
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A fan greets a king in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate; the question mark flags the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china, from china plate, rhymes with mate, meaning a pal.

clue.text: Christian, say, can always sustain character overseas

indicators.note: sustain in a down clue means the lower pieces hold up the Greek letter

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from abroad
a tin is a can
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A believer may keep a foreign personality going for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a believer but is Fletcher Christian, leader of the mutiny on HMS Bounty; 'say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian led the 1789 mutiny on the Bounty, making him the archetypal rebel against a ship's captain.

clue.text: Stoned bachelor by soldiers' house

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree
house, or housey-housey, was the forces' name for the numbers game also called lotto, the forerunner of bingo

explanation.surface: An unmarried man on drugs is next to the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the pieces side by side. 'house' looks like a building but is the old army name for the game of lotto or bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, and stoned can mean heavily intoxicated by drink or drugs.

clue.text: Gift more than one of 16 took to Tahiti?

definitions.text: more than one of 16 took to Tahiti?
definitions.meaning: the ship whose rebel crew sailed to Tahiti after the 1789 mutiny

explanation.walkthrough: 16 is MUTINEER, so 'more than one of 16' means the mutineers, who sailed HMS Bounty back to Tahiti.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounty is a generous gift, and HMS Bounty was the ship the mutineers took to Tahiti.

clue.text: Visionary Parisian who beheaded alien

parts.note: qui is French for who, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the alien word is cut off

parts.note: exotic means foreign or alien

explanation.surface: A dreamer from Paris who decapitated a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the E from EXOTIC, leaving XOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Quixotic, after Don Quixote, means idealistic and impractical, the outlook of a visionary dreamer.

clue.text: Church has inclination to go in for purge

indicators.note: to go in tells us the tilting word sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
leans means has an inclination or tilt

explanation.surface: A church tends to take part in a cleansing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go in' puts the inclination word inside the two church letters; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to purify or rid of dirt or sin, a verb synonym of purge.

clue.text: Put out about new hurt? It's causing no distress

indicators.note: about means the rearranged first word goes round the second
out signals that the letters of Put are rearranged
hurt signals the letters of new are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed about a fresh injury claims it doesn't upset them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT to UPT and 'hurt' rearranges the letters of 'new'; 'about' wraps the first result round the second. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss that is unwept is not mourned or grieved over, so it brings nobody sorrow.

clue.text: Ridiculous-sounding figure resistant to chemical attack

indicators.note: sounding says the word for ridiculous is pronounced like the start of the entry

parts.note: silly means ridiculous; said aloud it gives the opening sound of the entry
a cone is a solid geometric figure

explanation.surface: An absurd-sounding shape stands up to chemical damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, the words for ridiculous and figure make 'silly cone', the sound of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone polymers are prized for being inert, withstanding heat and chemicals, so the definition describes the substance by its property.

clue.text: Beetle, for example, giving East End bloke a turn?

parts.note: in Cockney speech him is said 'im, so a bloke there is 'im
a go is a turn, as in your go

explanation.surface: An insect lets a Cockney chap have a try.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End is the home of Cockney speech, which drops the H. 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult stage of an insect, so a grown beetle is one example.

clue.text: Possibly the sole counter in various games

definitions.meaning: the sole is one example of a flatfish
a token used for scoring in card games

explanation.definitionFit: The sole is a kind of fish, and in some card games a fish is a counter or token.

clue.text: Revolutionary device that has its purpose, one's admitted

definitions.text: Revolutionary device that has its purpose, one's admitted

parts.words: Revolutionary device that has its purpose, one's admitted
parts.note: a rotating gate whose whole job is to let people through one at a time

explanation.surface: A political radical's plot succeeds, someone confesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics but means rotating; 'one's admitted' sounds like a confession but means one person is let in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating barrier at a stadium or station lets people pass singly, admitting one per turn.

clue.text: Like a booby finding a way north?

parts.note: via means by way of

explanation.surface: A fool finds the road going north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booby' sounds like a fool but is a seabird related to the gannet. 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian means relating to birds, and the booby is a tropical seabird.

clue.text: Start to master different language from this?

definitions.text: Start to master different language from this?

indicators.note: start to asks for the opening letter of the word master

parts.note: other means different
tongue is another word for a language

explanation.surface: Learning a new language begins from the one you grew up with.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a definition: the language you begin from when learning another.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother tongue is the first language learnt in childhood, the base from which one learns others.
